steps.name: agents.expectDmRooms
steps.description: API: a DM room was created per member (the wizard's `dms` step). The room id round-trips through GET /api/matrix/agents.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: agents.expectDmRooms
    teamId: agentic-demos
    roleIds: [business-analyst, developer]

steps.name: agents.expectMembersRunning
steps.description: API: every member exists and is enabled (the orchestrator spawns a container for each enabled member — the UI shows this as the "Active" state). Polled because container spawn + Matrix provisioning settle shortly after `complete`.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id (with roleIds) to derive member ids.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: agents.expectMembersRunning
    teamId: agentic-demos
    roleIds: [business-analyst, developer]

steps.name: agents.expectTeamInRail
steps.description: UI: the team's group header and every member row are present in the Agent Chat left rail (`/chats`) — the surface that replaced the Agents page's team card in #1930.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id rendered as the rail's group header.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids (`<teamId>-<roleId>`).

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: agents.expectTeamInRail
    teamId: agentic-demos
    roleIds: [business-analyst, developer]

steps.name: chat.expectTriggerFired
steps.description: Assert that a github-event TRIGGER woke this agent, observed on the session SSE stream (#711 — "trigger fired = the agent's chat shows the trigger event via SSE"). The runtime appends a `trigger.fired` event to the session log at the head of every triggered run (agent-entrypoint.py `_execute_inner`); we subscribe to that agent's session stream from byte 0 and resolve on it. Self- contained: resolves the agent's DM room id itself (the trigger posts there), so the journey YAML only names the agentId. The stream endpoint holds the connection open even before the log file exists, so subscribing right after applying the label is safe (no lost event, no sleep).

params.name: agentId
params.description: Id of the agent expected to be woken by the trigger.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait for the trigger.fired event.

steps.name: chat.open
steps.description: Open an agent's DM chat and wait for the composer to be ready.

params.name: agentId
params.description: Id of the agent whose DM chat to open.

steps.name: chat.send
steps.description: Type a message and send it via the Send control (the same path a human uses; plain Enter is a newline, the button is disabled until the text is non-empty).

params.name: text
params.description: Message body to type and send.

steps.name: chat.waitForAgentReady
steps.description: Wait until the agent's RUNTIME is demonstrably up before sending the first message. The runtime drops any m.room.message whose origin_server_ts predates its own process start (agent-entrypoint.py, `ts < start_time_ms`) — so a send that races the container boot is silently ignored BY DESIGN, and F2 would time out without any product bug. `/api/agents/statuses` flips the agent from `offline` to `idle` exactly when the runtime has booted and pushed its status.json (#185) — after that point, a fresh message is inside the processing contract. Bounded poll, no sleeps beyond the interval tick.

params.name: agentId
params.description: Id of the agent whose runtime to wait for.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait for readiness.

steps.name: context.expectHostFile
steps.description: Assert a file REALLY landed in the hostPath by reading it back inside the kind node — the only vantage point that proves the write left the pod and hit the node filesystem (true end-to-end for the rw mount).
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: context.expectHostFile
    hostDir: /opt/e2e-context/specs
    name: notes.txt
    content: written through the console

steps.name: context.expectTreeEntry
steps.description: Poll the context BROWSE API until an entry appears in the tree — the first successful call proves the whole k8s chain: hostPath volume mounted in the agent pod, pods/exec transport up, containment guard passing. Polling (not a single call) absorbs the agent pod's startup window, during which the route honestly answers 409 agent-not-running.

params.name: agentId
params.description: Agent whose context tree to read.

params.name: name
params.description: Entry name expected in the listing.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: context.expectTreeEntry
    agentId: ctx-demo-agent
    path: specs
    name: brief.md

steps.name: context.openContextFile
steps.description: Expand a context root in the workspace tree and open a file in the viewer — the #1286 browse surface, rendered from data that travelled hostPath → pods/exec → orchestrator → console.

params.name: rootLabel
params.description: The mount's display name in the tree.

params.name: fileName
params.description: File row to click inside it.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: context.openContextFile
    rootLabel: specs
    fileName: brief.md
    contentSnippet: seeded on the kind node

steps.name: context.openWorkspacePanel
steps.description: Open the agent chat's Workspace panel (right rail) — same rail-handling as triggers.openPanel: reopen a collapsed rail, follow the tab into the overflow menu on a narrow rail. The "Reload tree" control confirms the workspace browser rendered.

params.name: agentId
params.description: Agent whose chat page to open.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: context.openWorkspacePanel
    agentId: ctx-demo-agent

steps.name: context.removeHostDir
steps.description: Remove a seeded directory from the kind node (fixture teardown helper).

steps.name: context.seedHostDir
steps.description: Seed a directory with one file inside the kind node (fixture helper — the hostPath a context mount binds must exist ON THE NODE before the agent pod starts, or the pod hangs Pending on FailedMount).

params.name: fileName
params.description: Seed file to write inside it.

steps.name: context.uploadFile
steps.description: Upload a generated file into a read-write context folder through the real console API (multipart, same route the workspace browser's upload panel posts to) — end-to-end this exercises the k8s WRITE path: prepare-upload exec, then the tar streamed over pods/exec stdin into the hostPath.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: context.uploadFile
    agentId: ctx-demo-agent
    dir: specs
    name: notes.txt
    content: written through the console

steps.name: create.expandAdvanced
steps.description: Expand the launcher's "Advanced options" disclosure, revealing the manual agent form entry. Idempotent — a second call on an already-open disclosure leaves it open rather than toggling it shut, so a journey can call it without tracking state.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: create.expandAdvanced

steps.name: create.expectEntry
steps.description: Assert a specific launcher entry is present with its visible heading. Lets a journey spot-check the plainly-labelled wording without clicking through. Expands the "Advanced options" disclosure first when the entry lives behind it, so a caller need not know which tier an entry is in.

params.name: entry
params.description: Which entry: chat | template | describe | build | single-agent.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: create.expectEntry
    entry: template

steps.name: create.open
steps.description: Open the unified "Create" launcher and confirm the ranked entries are showing: the hero, the three grouped flow cards, and the collapsed "Advanced options" disclosure (whose entry is deliberately NOT on screen yet). This is the single front door for starting something — the capture point for the launcher screenshot.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: create.open

steps.name: create.previewEntry
steps.description: Reveal an entry's "what you get" preview via its eye control (#2027) and confirm the schematic and its caption are showing. The control is the touch path — hover and keyboard focus reveal the same panel — and it is a sibling of the card's link, so clicking it previews instead of navigating. This step asserts exactly that: the preview appears AND we are still on the launcher. Only the three flow entries have a preview (#2034 dropped it from the hero and the advanced entry), so `entry` must be one of `template` / `describe` / `build` — the other two carry no eye control to click.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: create.previewEntry
    entry: template

steps.name: create.startFromTemplate
steps.description: From the launcher, take the "Start from a ready-made team" path: click that card and wait until the Team-Setup wizard's Process step (the template gallery) has loaded. Replaces the old direct `/team-setup` deep link so the journey exercises the real entry point users now take.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: create.startFromTemplate

steps.name: env.createFixtureEnv
steps.description: Create a Working Environment pointing at the in-stack git-remote fixture repo. Credential-less on purpose: no sshKeyId, no githubTokenId — the orchestrator clones `http://git-remote/…` anonymously and the poller ignores a token-less env, so the team materialises with zero external dependencies.

params.name: id
params.description: Slug id for the new environment.

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: env.createFixtureEnv
    id: agentic-demos-env
    name: Agentic Demos
    repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"

steps.name: env.createFixtureToken
steps.description: Create a GitHub token so the poller will poll the fixture repo (#711). The value is a syntactically-valid but fake PAT — the in-stack fake-github ignores auth entirely; it only needs to EXIST so `env.githubTokenId` resolves and the repo enters the poll plan. Idempotent via a fixed id (409 = already there).

params.name: id
params.description: Slug id for the token (referenced by the env).

steps.name: env.deleteEnv
steps.description: Idempotent teardown — 204 (deleted) and 404 (already gone) are both success, so a re-run or a partially-failed spec leaves no environment behind.

params.name: id
params.description: Id of the environment to delete.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: env.deleteEnv
    id: agentic-demos-env

steps.name: env.deleteFixtureToken
steps.description: Idempotent token teardown — 204 (deleted) and 404 (already gone) are success.

params.name: id
params.description: Id of the GitHub token to delete.

steps.name: flows.addAgentFromScratch
steps.description: Add an agent from scratch in one call: open the panel, optionally generate the prompt, and confirm. Composes openAddAgent + generateAgentPrompt + confirmAddAgent for steps that don't need to capture the intermediate panel states.

params.name: name
params.description: Agent display name (its node id is the slug).

params.name: notes
params.description: One-line intent used to generate the prompt.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.addAgentFromScratch
    name: Developer
    notes: Take an issue and implement it. Create a PR at the end.
    generate: true

steps.name: flows.addArtifactInput
steps.description: S11 — wire a file-artifact hand-off from the consumer side: Routing → Add input → File artifact → pick the producer → name the artifact.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.addArtifactInput
    name: Developer
    from: Analyst
    artifact: Analysis report

steps.name: flows.addHuman
steps.description: Add a named human role via the toolbar's Human-roles registry panel (#987) and close the panel.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.addHuman
    name: Product Owner

steps.name: flows.addOutcome
steps.description: Add one outcome on the open Routing tab (#828): title, optional `when`, and the label it sets. Does NOT save (batched into flows.saveOutcomes). Leave `label` empty for a terminal (no-signal) outcome.

params.name: title
params.description: Outcome title (its persisted id is the slug).

params.name: label
params.description: Label the outcome sets; empty = no signal.

params.name: action
params.description: Action type when not a label: "openPr", "openIssue" or "none" (#1010).

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.addOutcome
    name: Dispatcher
    title: Route to Developer
    when: Frontend/UI task
    label: ready

steps.name: flows.addRejectionPath
steps.description: S10 — add the rejection path in the OPEN Review-gate editor: on rejection, the producer is woken with this label. Closes the editor.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.addRejectionPath
    label: rework

steps.name: flows.addScheduleInput
steps.description: S8 — add a recurring schedule via Routing → Add input → Schedule (the shared trigger form; schedules have no canvas actor).
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.addScheduleInput
    name: Triage
    time: "07:00"
    prompt: Daily backlog sweep.

steps.name: flows.addStage
steps.description: Add an ordered stage to the draft (Stages dialog → "Add" → PUT). Stages are an organising layer; nodes are assigned to them in the node inspector.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.addStage
    name: Requirements

steps.name: flows.assignStage
steps.description: Assign an agent node to a stage via its inspector (Details → "Stage (layout column)" → Save). Opens the node, sets the stage, persists (PUT).

params.name: name
params.description: Agent display name whose node to assign.

params.name: stage
params.description: Stage name to assign it to.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.assignStage
    name: Business Analyst
    stage: Requirements

steps.name: flows.captureDraftWiring
steps.description: Capture the open draft's normalized wiring state under a name, for a later flows.expectDraftWiringEqual — the UI-level convergence check (concept §4.5).

params.name: as
params.description: Name to store the snapshot under.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.captureDraftWiring
    as: pathA

steps.name: flows.closeInspector
steps.description: Close the open node inspector panel by its agent display name.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.closeInspector
    name: Builder

steps.name: flows.closeStages
steps.description: Close the Stages dialog (its overlay would otherwise cover the canvas for a screenshot).
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.closeStages

steps.name: flows.confirmAddAgent
steps.description: Confirm the open Add-agent panel (→ PUT /api/process/drafts/:id) and wait for the new node to appear on the canvas.

params.name: name
params.description: Agent display name being added (its node slug).

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.confirmAddAgent
    name: Business Analyst

steps.name: flows.deleteReviewGate
steps.description: Delete the whole review gate from the open Review-gate editor (atomic, symmetric cleanup — §4.4).
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.deleteReviewGate

steps.name: flows.expectAgentCount
steps.description: Assert exactly `count` agent nodes are on the canvas (actor source nodes are a different class and are excluded).
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectAgentCount
    count: 2

steps.name: flows.expectAgentNode
steps.description: Assert an agent node is on the canvas by display name.

params.name: name
params.description: Agent display name whose node must be present.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectAgentNode
    name: Developer

steps.name: flows.expectAgentTriggerApi
steps.description: LIVE-mode wiring assertion: the member's persisted triggers.json (via the API) carries exactly one claimed single-event listener on the label — D1/D3 in live-team mode.

params.name: agentId
params.description: Full member agent id, e.g. wiring-demo-developer.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectAgentTriggerApi
    agentId: wiring-demo-developer
    event: issues.labeled
    labelFilter: ready

steps.name: flows.expectDraftSourceInputs
steps.description: S1/S8/S13 — assert the draft persists all three source inputs on a role: a raw github-event trigger, a cron schedule, and an http webhook.

params.name: role
params.description: Role display name (or id) in the draft.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectDraftSourceInputs
    role: Triage

steps.name: flows.expectDraftTrigger
steps.description: Assert the open draft persists EXACTLY ONE github-event listener with the given labelFilter on a role — single-event (D1) and, when `claimed`, the derived claim convention (D3): { remove: <label>, add: "<label>:wip" }.

params.name: role
params.description: Role display name (or id) in the draft.

params.name: labelFilter
params.description: The wake label the listener waits on.

params.name: claimed
params.description: Assert the derived claim is stamped.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectDraftTrigger
    role: Developer
    event: issues.labeled
    labelFilter: ready
    claimed: true

steps.name: flows.expectDraftWiringEqual
steps.description: Assert two captured wiring snapshots are identical — the concept's §4.5 convergence guarantee at UI level: different assembly orders must persist the same state.
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectDraftWiringEqual
    a: pathA
    b: pathB

steps.name: flows.expectEmptyDraft
steps.description: Assert the empty draft is on screen (capture point for the empty-draft screenshot): the from-scratch design hint + a zero-node canvas.
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectEmptyDraft

steps.name: flows.expectHandsOffLine
steps.description: S9 — assert an outcome hands off to a person: the Routing row reads "hands off to a person 👤".
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectHandsOffLine
    name: Reviewer

steps.name: flows.expectHumanNode
steps.description: Assert a named human renders as a human box on the canvas (#987).
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectHumanNode
    name: Product Owner

steps.name: flows.expectInputClaim
steps.description: S2 — assert the CLAIM BADGE renders on the canvas: the hand-off's edge chip reads "<label> · … ⇥ wip" (#958), so a claimed listener is visibly different from an unclaimed one.

params.name: label
params.description: The wake label whose claim chip must show.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectInputClaim
    label: ready

steps.name: flows.expectIssueChannel
steps.description: Assert the persisted draft carries the issue channel (consumer role has a `channels[]` entry from the producer with the routing label + human gate). API-level so it does not depend on canvas edge rendering.
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectIssueChannel
    from: Business Analyst
    to: Developer
    label: ready

steps.name: flows.expectLint
steps.description: Assert a lint code's presence or absence via the canvas lint panel (matched by the code's rendered plain-language title — see LINT_TITLES). With `absent: true` the whole lint button may be gone (fully clean) or the code missing from the open list.

params.name: absent
params.description: Assert the code does NOT fire.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectLint
    code: producer-unconsumed

steps.name: flows.expectMaterializeAvailable
steps.description: Assert the Materialize action is available on the draft (capture point for the finished-draft screenshot). The journey deliberately does not click it — a pure draft has no team side effects.
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectMaterializeAvailable

steps.name: flows.expectNoLints
steps.description: Assert the canvas shows NO lint issues — a clean flow renders no lint button at all (the Flows editor has no "clean" banner by design).
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectNoLints

steps.name: flows.expectNoOutcomes
steps.description: Assert the persisted draft role has NO authored outcomes port — the "decline persists nothing" check after a suggestion that was not saved (#828).
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectNoOutcomes
    name: Developer

steps.name: flows.expectOutcome
steps.description: Assert the persisted draft role carries an authored outcomes port with the given option id (and, optionally, mode). API-level, so it doesn't depend on canvas rendering.

params.name: outcomeId
params.description: Expected outcome option id (slug of its title).

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectOutcome
    name: Dispatcher
    outcomeId: route-to-developer
    mode: exactlyOne

steps.name: flows.expectOutcomeReviewer
steps.description: D4 — assert an outcome row of the open agent's Routing tab shows the "reviewed by 👤 <reviewer>" consumer line instead of a false "no consumer".
steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectOutcomeReviewer
    name: Business Analyst
    reviewer: Product Owner

steps.name: flows.expectReviewGate

params.name: reviewer
params.description: The named human of the triangle.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectReviewGate
    gateLabel: ready
    reviewer: Product Owner

steps.name: flows.expectSwitchNode
steps.description: Assert a node renders as a switch on the canvas — the ◇ switch badge (#828).

params.name: name
params.description: Agent display name whose node must show the badge.

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: flows.expectSwitchNode
    name: Dispatcher

steps.name: flows.generateAgentPrompt
steps.description: Press "Generate agent prompt" (→ POST /api/agent-prompt/generate; the mock LLM in the E2E stack answers) and wait for the generated prose to land in the editable Agent-prompt textarea (capture point for the generated-prompt panel). Requires the Add-agent panel open with a name filled.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.generateAgentPrompt

steps.name: flows.markOutcomeTerminal
steps.description: Open-end declaration (§4.7): mark an outcome of the open Routing tab terminal ("the end product") and assert the endpoint readout replaces the "no consumer yet" call-to-action. Leaves the inspector open.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.markOutcomeTerminal

steps.name: flows.newDraft

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.newDraft

params.name: name
params.description: Agent display name (its node id is the slug).

params.name: notes
params.description: One-line intent used to generate the prompt.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.openAddAgent
    name: Business Analyst
    notes: Take requirements and create a GitHub issue.

steps.name: flows.openReviewGate
steps.description: Open the one Review-gate editor (§4.4) by clicking the triangle's edge chip for the gate label.

params.name: gateLabel
params.description: The gate label of the triangle.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.openReviewGate
    gateLabel: ready

steps.name: flows.openRouting
steps.description: Open a node's Routing tab in the inspector (#828): click the node, then the Routing tab. Waits for the Outcomes heading.

params.name: name
params.description: Agent display name whose node to open.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.openRouting
    name: Dispatcher

steps.name: flows.openTeamFlow
steps.description: Open a LIVE team's flow graph from the Flows left list.
steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.openTeamFlow
    team: Wiring Demo

steps.name: flows.renameDraft
steps.description: Rename the open draft (inline title editor → PUT /api/process/drafts/:id). The fixed name is what the fixture pre-/post-cleans on, keeping the journey re-runnable.
steps.example:

steps.name: flows.saveOutcomes

    name: Dispatcher

steps.name: flows.setLabelBrake
steps.description: S9 — flag a routing label as a Brake (flow → person) in the Label registry; the outcome that sets it then reads "hands off to a person".
steps.example:

steps.name: flows.setOutcomeMode
steps.description: Set the outcome mode on the open Routing tab (#828): the switch (exactly one) or any-of. The two radios are ordered exactly-one, any-of.

params.name: name

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.setOutcomeMode
    name: Dispatcher
    mode: exactlyOne

steps.name: flows.showStages
steps.description: Turn ON the canvas stage-band view so a screenshot shows the assigned agents grouped into labelled bands (the state the flows-draft narrative describes), instead of the ungrouped graph. Two "Stages" controls exist: the first (in the top action bar) opens the StageManager dialog (cf. addStage); the second is the canvas band-toggle. Clicks the band-toggle and waits for a band header to render. Idempotent-ish: if the bands are already shown it is a no-op click guarded by the header check.

params.description: A stage name expected to appear

    do: flows.showStages

steps.name: flows.suggestOutcomes
steps.description: Press "Suggest outcomes…" on the open Routing tab (#828) → POST /api/agent-outcomes/suggest (mock LLM in the E2E stack, heuristic fallback).     do: flows.suggestOutcomes

steps.name: flows.wireGithubSource
steps.description: S1 — wire a raw GitHub event source: drag @github onto an agent, pick "GitHub trigger", choose the event (+ optional label filter).

steps.name: flows.wireHumanDelivery
steps.description: S3 path B, first leg — drag a producer agent onto a human box: "P reviews A's work" (delivery only; the wake stays unwired for the second leg).

- action:
    do: flows.wireHumanDelivery
    from: Business Analyst
    human: Product Owner

steps.name: flows.wireHumanDeliveryFromOutcome
steps.description: S3 path B, first leg via the OUTCOME PORT: drag the producer's outcome port (e.g. "Opens issue") onto a human box. Must open the person-delivery dialog ("P reviews A's work") — never the channel form (the #1010 regression: the pre-typed outcome drag used to mis-wire the person as a channel role).

params.description: The outcome port's title, e.g. "Opens issue".

- action:
    do: flows.wireHumanDeliveryFromOutcome
    from: Business Analyst

steps.name: flows.wireHumanGate
steps.description: S3 path B, second leg — drag a human box onto a consumer agent: "P approves → B wakes". Artifact kind is inferred/selected; claim is stamped by the engine. Optionally wires the S10 rejection path back to the producer.

params.name: rejectionLabel
params.description: When set, enable "On rejection, wake <producer>" with this label.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: flows.wireHumanGate
    human: Product Owner
    to: Developer
    label: ready

steps.name: flows.wireIssueChannel
steps.description: Wire an Issue channel from one agent to another with a human-approval gate: drag the producer's port onto the consumer, choose "Issue channel", enter the routing label, tick the human-approval gate, and create it (→ PUT /api/process/drafts/:id). The gate requires a routing label (product rule).

params.name: from
params.description: Producer agent display name (opens the issue).

params.name: to

fixtures.name: contextMountAgent
fixtures.description: contextMountAgent: the context-mount journey's precondition (#1319). KIND-LANE ONLY — the mount is a k8s hostPath, so "host" is the kind node container: setup shells into it (docker/podman exec from the Playwright host, the same engine that runs the kind provider) to seed the folder, then stands up one standalone agent on a repo-less env and sets a READ-WRITE multi-folder context mount via the real PATCH route (#1290 shape — the folder gets a slug and mounts at /context/<slug> in the agent pod). The agent is enabled last; the journey's first browse poll absorbs the pod startup window. ENSURE, NEVER DELETE: deleting an agent deactivates its Matrix user, and a conduwuit deactivation is permanent — recreating the same fixed id then fails with M_USER_DEACTIVATED. So setup treats an existing agent/env as reusable (409 = fine) and teardown only DISABLES the agent (pod gone, node folder removable) — same lifecycle as stack-up.sh's standalone e2e-agent. The pre-clean also disables first: re-seeding the node folder while a live pod bind-mounts it would leave that pod staring at the deleted inode.

params.name: hostDir
params.description: Absolute folder path INSIDE the kind node.

params.name: seedFile
params.description: File seeded into the folder before mount.

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: contextMountAgent
    params:
      agentId: ctx-demo-agent
      envId: ctx-demo-env
      envName: Context Demo
      hostDir: /opt/e2e-context/specs
      mountName: specs
      seedFile: brief.md
      seedContent: "Context briefing — seeded on the kind node."

fixtures.name: flowsDraft
fixtures.description: flowsDraft: the `flows-draft` journey's precondition (#733). The journey authors a draft named `draftName` and never materialises it, so there is no team/env/Matrix state — only the draft document. This fixture just pre-/post- cleans any draft with that name so a re-run (or a crashed prior run) starts and ends clean.

params.name: draftName
params.description: Draft name the journey renames to.

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: flowsDraft
    params:
      draftName: Simple SDLC

fixtures.name: ibanStoryTeam
fixtures.description: ibanStoryTeam: the IBAN-story journey's precondition (#711). Stands up the WHOLE label-chain stack in one atomic precondition so the journey body only drives the hops: it (1) resets fake-github so the run starts from clean GitHub state, (2) creates a fake GitHub token so the poller actually polls the fixture repo (a token-less env is ignored by the poller), (3) creates a credential-carrying Working Environment pointing at the in-stack git remote, and (4) materialises a full Core SDLC team FROM THE PROCESS-TEMPLATE BUNDLE — so `POST /api/teams` runs `expandGithubChannels` and the Developer/Code-Reviewer get the derived github-event channel triggers (issues.labeled=`ready`, pull_request.labeled= `ready-for-review`) that carry the label chain. Bare `roles` would materialise the same agents WITHOUT those channels. FIXED ids keep the journey re-runnable on the same stack: setup pre-cleans any leftover team+env+token from a crashed prior run, and teardown removes the team, env and token this journey created — one deterministic, idempotent surface.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id to create (also its member prefix).

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at (the in-stack git remote).

params.name: tokenId
params.description: Fixture GitHub-token id (referenced by the env).

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: ibanStoryTeam
    params:
      teamId: iban-demo
      teamName: IBAN Demo
      envId: iban-demo-env
      envName: IBAN Demo
      repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"
      tokenId: iban-demo-token

fixtures.name: knowledgeTeam
fixtures.description: knowledgeTeam: the Knowledge-chapter journey's precondition (#1784). Gives the /knowledge page deterministic content to show WITHOUT depending on any agent having actually run (a fresh team has learned nothing yet): it (1) seeds a global-pool skill so the team-flow's skills lane and the activation beat have a real skill to activate, (2) creates a credential-less Working Environment on the in-stack git remote (no external deps), and (3) materialises a small two-member team (BA + Developer) so the page shows a real team with real members — enough to prove member-level activation on the activation beat. Composes the existing #668 fixture steps (knowledge.createGlobalSkill, env.createFixtureEnv, team.materializeTeam) — no duplicate logic. FIXED ids keep the screenshots deterministic (§7): setup pre-cleans a leftover team+env and the pool skill from a crashed prior run, and teardown removes the team, env and skill this journey created — one idempotent, re-runnable surface.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id to create (also its member prefix).

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at (the in-stack git remote).

params.name: skillName
params.description: Global-pool skill to seed and activate on the team.

params.name: roles
params.description: Catalog role ids for the members.

fixtures.example:

  - fixture: knowledgeTeam
    params:
      teamId: knowledge-demo
      envId: knowledge-demo-env
      envName: Knowledge Demo
      repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"
      skillName: iban-validation

fixtures.description: liveWiringTeam: the review-gate-live journey's precondition (#1010). A MINIMAL live team (Business Analyst + Developer) materialised from an inline bundle on a credential-less env pointing at the in-stack git remote — enough for the Flow editor's live scope to wire a review gate against real member configs, with no GitHub polling (token-less env) and no label chain to run. FIXED ids: setup pre-cleans a leftover team+env; teardown removes both.

fixtures.name: triggerAgent
fixtures.description: triggerAgent: the `triggers` journey's precondition (#733). Stands up ONE Business-Analyst agent to hang triggers on, as cheaply as possible: a credential-less Working Environment plus a single-member team. The env's repository URL is deliberately a github.com URL so the trigger panel's repo picker (parseRepoFullName, github.com-only) offers it for the github-event / data-flow trigger types — while the token-less HTTPS clone is refused fast by the orchestrator (no PAT ⇒ no username-prompt hang) and tolerated as a seed warning, so the member still materialises. No token ⇒ the poller ignores the repo, so nothing the journey configures ever fires: the config tour stays deterministic (github-event firing end-to-end is already covered by the iban-story journey). FIXED ids keep it re-runnable: setup pre-cleans a leftover team+env, teardown removes the team (cascades to the member) + env.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id (its BA member is `<teamId>-business-analyst`).

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: github.com repo URL (parseable by the trigger repo picker).

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: triggerAgent
    params:
      teamId: triggers-demo
      envId: triggers-demo-env
      envName: Triggers Demo
      repoUrl: "https://github.com/aee-e2e/triggers-demo.git"

fixtures.name: usageData
fixtures.description: usageData: the Token Usage journey's precondition (#1505). Seeds deterministic usage records under a dedicated human Team and creates that Team, so the page's Team filter can narrow to it and the figures stay stable across re-runs on the same stack (other usage the stack logs carries a different teamId and is filtered out). Setup pre-cleans a leftover team + seed files; teardown removes both — one idempotent, re-runnable surface.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id to create and tag the seeded records with.

params.name: teamName
params.description: Team display name (shown in the page's Team filter).

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: usageData
    params:
      teamId: token-usage-demo
      teamName: Token Usage Demo
